article.title: Common mistake: 'from' vs 'since' for time
article.description: Wrong: 'I have lived here from 2015.' Right: 'I have lived here since 2015.' Teaching point: use 'since' with present perfect for a starting point still relevant now; 'from' is used with a defined start AND end point, like 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.'
article.content: Wrong: 'I have lived here from 2015.' Right: 'I have lived here since 2015.' Teaching point: use 'since' with present perfect for a starting point still relevant now; 'from' is used with a defined start AND end point, like 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.'

generated.caption:
Ever said "I've worked here from 2015" and felt something was off? 🤔 You're not alone!

Use 'since' with the present perfect to talk about a start point that continues to the present. For example: "I have lived here since 2015." 'From' needs a definite start AND end point, like "The offer is valid from Monday to Friday."

generated.script: Aapne bhi kabhi ye sentence bola hoga, "I have lived here from 2015"? Toh suno, ye galat hai! Correct sentence hai "I have lived here since 2015". "Since" hum use karte hain present perfect tense ke saath jab ek starting point abhi tak relevant ho. Matlab, 2015 se main abhi tak yahin reh raha hoon. Lekin "from"? "From" use hota hai jab ek defined start aur end point ho. Jaise, "The offer is valid from Monday to Friday". Toh next time jab bhi koi cheez past mein start hui ho aur abhi bhi chal rahi ho, use "since". Aur jab start aur end dono defined ho, tab "from". Ab samjha? Comment mein batao ye mistake aap bhi karte the kya! Aur follow karo The English Vault ko for more awesome English tips!

slides.body: Many English learners often confuse 'since' and 'from' when referring to time, especially with the present perfect tense. Remember, we use 'since' to indicate a starting point in the past that continues up to the present moment, like in the correct sentence: 'I have lived here since 2015.' Using 'from' here, as in 'I have lived here from 2015,' is incorrect. In contrast, 'from' is typically used when you specify both a clear starting point AND an ending point for a duration, for example: 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.' Mastering this distinction will significantly improve your accuracy when discussing time.
slides.hindiSummary: जब कोई कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर वर्तमान तक जारी रहे तो 'since' का प्रयोग करें, और जब शुरुआत व अंत दोनों बिंदु निश्चित हों तो 'from' का प्रयोग करें।
